newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London flat, turnover thin.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London flat, turnover thin.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks trading in London were mostly unchanged in very thin trade ahead of the weekend on Friday after the Hang Seng's dramatic surge overnight.
"The only price I've changed today is HongKong Bank," one dealer said. HSBC Holdings was up HK$1/2 from a close of HK$245.
Investors decided to take a breather and market-makers preferred to keep flat positions after the Hang Seng finished 386 points, or 2.6 percent, higher at 15,225.29.
The London Reference Index was up 0.44 points at 15,224.85.
"The market was very strong in Hong Kong today on short covering because a lot of people anticipated that the market would go down after the handover," a dealer said.
"There was a bear squeeze in Hong Kong but it didn't follow through to London."
Traders predicted the Hang Seng could make further progress after the weekend.
"When you see big movements in the market like this it doesn't usually happen for just one day," one said.
